context: Change the canonical source at /Users/joe/.skill-sync/skills, not generated project mirrors. Introduce stable policy identifiers and an authority-provenance vocabulary, add an explicit identity-preservation rule to the shared commit path, establish a mechanically checkable parity contract for compressed protocols, and extend permission auditing to conflicting executable policy.
description: Canonical shared skills do not explicitly require agents to preserve Git author and committer identity unless an authorized task names an override, and they do not consistently label whether a requirement comes from the current task, repository policy, a mechanical gate, or a recommendation. The compressed review protocol is also maintained in manual lockstep with a fuller BenchBox protocol, creating semantic-drift risk. These gaps contributed to ambiguous language such as required Claude author even when the actual authority was a one-off task step.

anti_patterns.instead: Edit the canonical skill source and materialize through skill-sync
anti_patterns.why: They are generated mirrors and will drift or be overwritten

anti_patterns.dont: Turn task-local identity instructions into a global Claude author rule
anti_patterns.instead: Preserve configured identity unless the current authorized task explicitly overrides it
anti_patterns.why: That would silently misattribute unrelated commits
